audit.why: Urgot owning levels 1, 3, 4-5 and late with Rumble taking only level 6 matches the 48.39% figure and the flow of the text. The difficulty framing needs no correction — only the numbers inside it do.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spike list is built on 'percent-max-HP Purge' — stated in spikes[2], spikes[3], whys[2] and whys[6] — and the late paragraph concludes from it that 'your HP pool is irrelevant'. Riot's text for Purge and for Echoing Flames describes physical damage and contains no percent-health component, and the kit library carries no percentHealth flag for Urgot on any ability. Separately, the real Purge spike is never mentioned: its cooldown falls 12/9/6/3/0, so at rank 5 it has no cooldown and no cost at all.
audit.why: The two-item spike drives the whole late plan, and it is currently attributed to a mechanic Riot's text does not describe, while the genuine, checkable spike — Purge becoming free and cooldown-less — is absent. Advice to 'back out before he can cycle a second Purge window' stops being possible once there is no cycle.
audit.corrected: His scaling spike is Purge reaching rank 5, where it costs nothing and has no cooldown, so there is no window between activations to retreat into. The damage is physical and comes off Echoing Flames, so armour is the stat that answers it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/urgot.json (Purge cd 12/9/6/3/0, cost 40/30/20/10/0; Echoing Flames 'dealing physical damage'; no percentHealth flag on any Urgot ability)

audit.whatIsWrong: Three interaction errors. (a) The early paragraph instructs the player to 'track his E cooldown (12 seconds)' — Disdain is 16/15.5/15/14.5/14, so 12 is not the value at any rank and the number is low, which is the dangerous direction to be wrong in. (b) Disdain also shields Urgot on the charge; the matchup treats it purely as a flip, so a Rumble who trades into it finds his burst absorbed. (c) The late paragraph says Fear Beyond Death 'will execute you if he ever catches you below half health with Disdain', tying the ultimate to the flip. Fear Beyond Death is an independent 2500-range chem-drill that impales the first champion hit; it needs no Disdain.
audit.why: Point 4 is the key point, and (a) is the worst kind of error to ship — a player counting to 12 steps up while Disdain still has four seconds left. (c) creates false safety: staying out of the 475-range flip does nothing about a 2500-range ultimate.
audit.corrected: Disdain is 16s at rank 1 and shields him as he charges, so it is both his engage and part of his effective health — bait it, then trade. Fear Beyond Death reaches 2500 units on its own and does not need the flip; the low-health threshold is what to respect, not the distance.
sources: champ-data/_kits/urgot.json (Disdain cd 16/15.5/15/14.5/14, range 475, flags hardCC + shield, 'charges in a direction, shielding himself'; Fear Beyond Death range 2500, execute)

audit.whatIsWrong: Because Purge is described as dealing 'percent-max-HP magic damage', the itemization implied by the matchup points at magic resist and away from health. Riot's text puts the damage on Echoing Flames as physical.
audit.why: This is the practical consequence of the point-4 error: it sends the player to the wrong resistance.
audit.corrected: Armour, not magic resist, is the answer to Purge. Health is not wasted here either, once the percent-max-HP framing is dropped.

edits.before: At level 1 Urgot's Q (Corrosive Charge) is a ranged slow-projectile he throws from outside Flamespitter range — he uses it to chip you and then walk away before you can retaliate with Q. Do not rush at him; let him push the wave and Q at him only when he steps up for a last-hit. At level 2 you can Q into double-E-slow to punish an overextension, but his E flip is also online — if he lands Disdain, you eat a full Purge burst at point-blank and your W shield barely covers it. Play around a creep wall so he cannot flip through minions cleanly, and track his E cooldown (12 seconds) before committing anything.
edits.after: At level 1 Urgot's Q (Corrosive Charge) is a ranged slow-projectile he throws from outside Flamespitter range — he uses it to chip you and then walk away before you can retaliate with Q. Do not rush at him; let him push the wave and Q at him only when he steps up for a last-hit. At level 2 you can Q into double-E-slow to punish an overextension, but his E flip is also online — Disdain shields him as he charges, so it is his engage and his health bar at once. Play around a creep wall so he cannot flip through minions cleanly, and track Disdain properly: 16 seconds at rank 1, not twelve.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are Urgot's sustained-trade window — his Purge (W) deals percent-max-HP magic damage and simply out-DPSes your Danger Zone Flamespitter in a prolonged fight. Trade short: walk Flamespitter through him at 50-100 Heat, double-E-slow if he tries to stick, pop W shield to absorb the immediate Purge burst, then back out before he can cycle a second Purge window. Never let him flip you when Flamespitter is already channeling — the silence from your own Overheat on top of a flip is a death sentence. At level 6 the math shifts: threaten Equalizer across his E path and he has to play extremely respectfully around river, giving you free waves and pressure.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are Urgot's sustained-trade window — Purge (W) is physical damage off his Echoing Flames legs and out-DPSes your Danger Zone Flamespitter in any prolonged fight. Trade short: walk Flamespitter through him at 50-100 Heat, double-E-slow if he tries to stick, pop W shield for the burst, then leave — and note the cycle shrinks every rank, 12 seconds down to none at rank 5. Never let him flip you when Flamespitter is already channeling — your own Overheat silence on top of a flip is a death sentence. At level 6 the math shifts: threaten Equalizer across his E path and he must respect river, giving you free waves.

edits.before: Past two items Urgot's percent-max-HP Purge is genuinely unanswerable in a straight duel — your HP pool is irrelevant, and your W shield regenerates too slowly to keep up with his sustained fire. Do not fight him alone. Your job is Equalizer: throw it across chokes, Baron pit, and Dragon to zone him and your entire team gets free damage on a champion with no mobility. His Fear Beyond Death (R) will execute you if he ever catches you below half health with Disdain — stay topped up and never let him land the flip when you are low.
edits.after: Past two items Purge has no cooldown and no cost at rank 5, so there is no gap between activations to retreat into — that, not your HP pool, is what makes the duel unwinnable. Do not fight him alone. Your job is Equalizer: throw it across chokes, Baron pit, and Dragon to zone him and your entire team gets free damage on a champion with no mobility. Fear Beyond Death reaches 2500 units on its own and needs no flip to land — respect the health threshold, not the distance, and stay topped up.

notes: Both packet suspectNames are false positives. The substantive defects were numeric and elemental. (1) 'track his E cooldown (12 seconds)' is wrong at every rank — Disdain is 16/15.5/15/14.5/14 — and it errs low, which sends the player forward while the flip is still up. (2) 'percent-max-HP Purge' appears four times and drives the late-game conclusion that 'your HP pool is irrelevant'; Riot's text for Purge and Echoing Flames describes physical damage with no percent-health component, and no Urgot ability carries a percentHealth flag in the kit library. I replaced the framing with the spike that is verifiable — Purge reaching rank 5 with zero cost and zero cooldown — and marked the percent-health question as unverified rather than asserting the negative. If the user has a source confirming a percent-health component on Purge, these four lines are where it belongs. (3) 'his Urgot's Fear Beyond Death' in wants.foe[2] is a doubled possessive, and the late paragraph wrongly gates the 2500-range ultimate behind the 475-range flip.
